lessons.title: Bulk provisioning — validate before import
lessons.why: A CSV is input data, not authorization. The portal validates the latest exact template; each row represents a proposed user. Use the actual template for an authorized tenant, unique temporary credentials through a protected process, and account-state review. Never upload shared sample passwords.
lessons.example: Preview four fictional requests: Ava (ava@lab.example, Sales, US); Bo (bo@lab.example, Finance, US); duplicate AVA@lab.example (Marketing, US); Chen (chen@unverified.example, Support, US). The only approved suffix is lab.example. No password is stored in this planning exercise.
lessons.question: Which rows are eligible to proceed to authorized creation, and what must happen before assigning licenses?
lessons.answer: Ava and Bo are valid planning rows, not created users. Reject the duplicate UPN case-insensitively and unverified domain. Obtain individual secure credentials, verify required fields using the current template, confirm usage location and available license seats, validate and inspect per-row results. A failed row does not establish that every other row failed.

lessons.title: Privacy notice versus access policy
lessons.why: A tenant privacy statement tells people how data is handled and a contact identifies a responsible channel. A notice URL does not grant access, enforce MFA, or replace legal-approved disclosure. Do not upload the example PDF as a real notice.
lessons.example: A guest sees a review-permissions page with no organization privacy URL. The fictional administrator has a reviewed notice and privacy contact.
lessons.question: Which property change addresses missing notice information, and what evidence confirms success without granting new resource access?
lessons.answer: An authorized administrator sets the approved privacy statement URL and contact in tenant properties. Verify the URL is reachable and the intended notice is visible in a test guest/user view. Resource access remains controlled by assignments and policy; do not change them to fix the notice.

lessons.title: Hybrid directory seed data — safe provisioning design
lessons.why: Directory seeding is a change operation. The upstream demo script weakens domain security and performs broad privileged actions; it is excluded. An OU organizes objects and can scope GPO or synchronization; a security group grants access through assignments; neither should be conflated with an admin role. A source anchor identifies a synchronized identity independently of display name and UPN.
lessons.example: Use three fictional records only: Ava, Sales, OU=Sales; Bo, IT Support, OU=Support; Chen, Finance, OU=Finance. Each has a unique planned sign-in name. Existing domain password policy is unchanged, all privileged group grants are absent, and no real password is collected. Preview intended add operations, existing-object collisions, destination OUs, and group memberships before any approved write.
lessons.question: A script proposes deleting an existing OU, disabling password complexity, nesting all IT staff in Domain Admins, then creating 1,000 users. Which operations should be approved for this exercise?
lessons.answer: None of those writes are needed or authorized. Keep the existing OU and policy unchanged; reject the privileged nesting and bulk creation. Teach only bounded synthetic records and explicit nonprivileged membership. An authorized real lab could inspect existing AD objects and password policy read-only, then perform narrowly scoped approved changes with validation, rollback and independent review. Do not run the source script.

lessons.title: Terms document lifecycle and acceptance evidence
lessons.why: Terms of use is an agreement object with a PDF/version and acceptance records; a Conditional Access grant requirement enforces it for an applicable sign-in. The same upstream sample appears twice and is not legally approved production content.
lessons.example: Fictional version 1 accepted by Ava. An approved version 2 changes the terms and requires reacceptance; Bo has never accepted. A policy targets the pilot group. An active session may not reevaluate immediately.
lessons.question: What should the administrator verify after version 2 is published, and how does this differ from the tenant privacy notice?
lessons.answer: Inspect the current document version and require-reaccept setting, scope and applicable licensed Conditional Access policy, then verify a fresh applicable sign-in prompts for the current agreement and the acceptance report records it. A decline prevents satisfying the required grant. Existing sessions and exclusions must be considered. A privacy notice URL alone is not an acceptance grant.
